question.problem: Let $A$ and $B$ be the set of all multiples of $4$ greater than $0$ and the set of all multiples of $5$ greater than $0,$ respectively. What is $A\cup B?$
question.worked_solution:
The multiples of $4$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
A=\{4,8,12,16,20,…\}.
$$

Likewise, multiples of $5$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
B=\{5,10,15,20,…\}.
$$

Now, $A\cup B$ is the *union* of $A$ and $B,$ which means that we want to find the elements that are in either $A$ or $B,$ or both. In other words, $A\cup B$ denotes the set of natural numbers that are either multiple of $4$ or multiple of $5.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A\cup B & =\{4,8,12,16,20,…\}\cup \{5,10,15,20,…\} \\  & =\{4,5,8,10,12,15,16,20,…\}.\end{aligned}
$$
